items.title: Paving the Road to Production: Governed Enterprise AI Agents — Harish Gaggar, Credit Karma
items.summary: Register an agent through an internal portal and receive more than a repository: the deployment also needs identity, memory, traces, evaluations and secret handling. Harish Gaggar walks through that paved path for enterprise agents at Intuit Credit Karma. Local development progresses through container builds, review, security scanning and Kubernetes deployment, with the supporting resources provisioned consistently. The architecture places a centralized MCP gateway between agents and tools so authentication and routing are part of every request. Custom MCP servers expose reviewed tools, while OpenTelemetry, Tempo, Prometheus and Grafana make failures, latency and access behavior visible. Gaggar then follows a LangGraph workflow from interpretation and planning through evidence gathering, policy checks and human approval for sensitive actions. Threads, runs and checkpoints preserve state, while separate tracking tables record model use, tool calls, costs and evaluation fields. Demonstrations inspect those records rather than establish a validated quality score for the whole system. A PII filtering layer aims to intercept sensitive inputs before they reach models, memory or traces; detection and redaction remain controls to evaluate, rather than a guarantee that no secret can escape. The final component prunes, reranks, deduplicates and compresses context. Its examples show large token reductions, including about 90% in a demonstrated query, without a paired answer quality…

items.excerpt: # Claude Code Plugins Directory A curated directory of high-quality plugins for Claude Code. > **⚠️ Important:** Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information. ## Structure - **`/plugins`** - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic - **`/external_plugins`** - Third-party plugins from partners and the community ## Installation Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system. To install, run `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official` or browse for the plugin in `/plugin > Discover` ## Contributing ### Internal Plugins Internal plugins are developed by Anthropic team members. See `/plugins/example-plugin` for a reference implementation. ### External Plugins Third-party partners can submit plugins for inclusion in the marketplace. External plugins must meet quality and security standards for approval. items.title: akitaonrails / ai-memory
items.summary: Solution for long term memory for agent coding CLIs and to facilitate handoff between different agent vendors
items.excerpt: > Long-term memory for AI coding agents. Quit Claude Code mid-task, > start OpenAI Codex in the same directory, continue without > re-explaining the architecture, the failed approaches, or the open > questions. **Website: [aimemory.sh](https://aimemory.sh)** [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/website-aimemory.sh-blue)](https://aimemory.sh) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/akitaonrails/ai-memory)](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/releases/latest) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.95+-blue)](rust-toolchain.toml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ## Why ai-memory Your coding agent probably has a memory feature already. Claude Code takes its own notes, Cursor remembers some things, and every platform is adding more. They all have the same limits: the notes live on one machine, belong to one agent, and drop out of view when you switch tools or hand the work to a teammate. ai-memory removes those limits. - **It follows you across agents.** More than twenty harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Grok, Devin, Kimi, Kiro, and others) feed one shared memory. Quit Claude Code mid-task, open Codex in the same directory, and the next agent picks up a handoff that says where you left off, what failed, and what is still open. Handoffs are a typed protocol: each one has an owner and is claimed exactly once. - **It can carry the session, not just a summary.** Start agents with `ai-memory…
